headline: Errors are deviations from expectations—they reveal where reality differs from your model
universal_truth: Errors are information; they tell you where your understanding is incomplete; learning requires mistakes
fun_facts: Penicillin, X-rays, and Post-it notes were all discovered through errors
Airlines have become incredibly safe by treating every error as a learning opportunity, not a blame target
The brain learns most effectively when predictions are wrong—surprise is the engine of learning
discussion_questions: How do you typically respond to errors?
What's an error that taught you something valuable?
How could you create safer conditions for making mistakes?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You expected one thing; you got another. That gap—error—is information. It tells you your model is incomplete. Errors are unpleasant but invaluable: they're the only reliable way to update your understanding.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We treat errors as failures to avoid. But errors are often the best teachers. How should we relate to mistakes?
cliff.prompt: What's the right relationship to error?

options.text: Errors should be expected, examined, and learned from—they're information about where your model needs updating, not evidence of failure
options.response: Yes. Errors reveal the gap between expectation and reality. That's priceless feedback. The mistake isn't the error—it's not learning from it.
Prevention helps, but some errors are unavoidable and valuable—the key is learning from them...

q1.title: Errors as Information
q1.script: Every error reveals something: a flawed assumption, missing knowledge, unexpected condition. Before blaming or fixing, ask: what does this error teach me? The information is valuable.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Errors as Information"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Safe-to-Fail Environments
q2.script: Learning requires making mistakes. The best environments make it safe to fail—low stakes, fast feedback, no blame. Creating safe-to-fail conditions accelerates learning.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Error Prevention vs Recovery
q3.script: You can't prevent all errors—complexity guarantees surprises. What matters is quick detection and recovery. Build systems that catch errors early and respond gracefully.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Errors are information. They tell you where your understanding is incomplete. Learning requires mistakes—make them safely and learn from them.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 234. Tomorrow, we'll explore protecting what we have—preservation. Until then, examine a recent error for what it taught you.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Error Analysis - What Did It Teach?
growTrack.activity: Think of a recent error—something that didn't go as expected. Instead of dismissing or regretting it, analyze: what assumption was wrong? What did you learn? How will you adjust? Errors are tuition for learning.
